cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Build a Coalition
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Join my request to keep the pottery room open late. One name is a personal request; we need a properly represented proposal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why I need you. An evening-class petition only proves the evening class wants longer hours. Put your class beside your name, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The morning class wants weekend access.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then change the heading to 'Extended access' and bring their representative. One proposal, please; don't split our support into two little complaints.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 representative proposal, A3 class identification and A5 unified heading make professional drafting shape cross-class coalition recruitment.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 leaving at five explains lack of late-hours need; B4 weekend access can join late hours under extended access.

relationship.evidence: B2 disinterest and B4 useful alternative constituency materially change A request.

heightening.evidence: B4 weekend demand causes A5 broader heading and another representative, preserving one coalition.

specificity.evidence: A1 pottery room and B2 five oclock departure make the immediate support problem clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 heading and representative request are necessary coalition actions; final warning tells B not to fragment them.
